issues.body: In `scan_bare_words`, every `<` unconditionally enters the IRIREF-skipping branch. In SPARQL, `<` is also a comparison operator. For example, `SELECT ?s WHERE { ?s ?p ?o FILTER(?o < 1) FLTR(?o) }` reaches the parse-failure diagnostic, but the scanner starts at the comparison operator and advances to end-of-input because there is no later `>`, so it never reports `FLTR`. With a later greater-than comparison it instead swallows everything through that operator. This is a common query shape and contradicts the public claim that the scan finds bare words near SPARQL keywords while ignoring actual IRIs.
issues.fix_hint: Distinguish IRIREF starts from comparison operators using lexical context consistent with the SPARQL lexer, rather than treating every `<` as an IRI. Add an integration-level regression test containing a valid `<` comparison followed by `FLTR`, asserting that `CanaryFailed.suggestions` still contains `FILTER`; also cover a query with both `<` and `>` comparison operators.
issues.title: Less-than operators swallow the remainder of the query

verdict.summary: The diagnostic remains fail-closed and the integration test verifies that the emitted query is not rewritten. However, the new lexer conflates SPARQL's less-than comparison operator with the start of an IRIREF. This causes a common valid expression before a misspelled keyword to hide that typo from the diagnostic, so the advertised bare-word scan is incomplete on ordinary query text.
